data.name: Coral
data.gender_notes: Coral is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'korallion', meaning 'sea pink', 'coral' refers to the beautiful, hard, red or pink mineral deposit formed from tiny dead organisms in the ocean. In ancient Greece, coral was believed to be the heart of the sea and symbolized love, passion, and creativity. The name Coral carries the meaning “Gemstone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Coral usually hope their child will grow to embody gemstone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of love, creativity, and passion.
data.etymology: Coral belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gemstone.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Coral total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: In Christianity, the name "Coral" carries a beautiful cultural significance referring to the passion and love of Jesus Christ. The name represents the precious and valuable sacrifice He made for humanity when He willingly gave His life on the cross. Just as the coral is formed from the collective efforts of organisms in the ocean, so too is the Christian faith formed through the collective effort and love of believers. The name Coral evokes a sense of unity, strength, and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Coral" can be seen as a symbol of enduring love and sacrifice. It is a reminder of the love and sacrifice of Jesus Christ, whose life, death, and resurrection provides a foundation for our own spiritual journey. The name Coral also highlights the importance of community and unity among believers, as we come together to build a collective faith that is strong and resilient, much like the coral itself. Additionally, the name can be seen as a reminder of the power of the natural world and God's creation, and the beauty and mystery that can be found within it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Coral represents enduring love and connection, drawing strength from deep roots. It symbolizes the resilience of faith, thriving in the midst of life's challenges like the coral reef in the ocean. Note: This response is not based on any specific Christian tradition or scripture, but rather an interpretation drawn from the symbolic meaning of the word "coral" in general.
